chunks: From him, from his father, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, there is no throbbing vein, nor a calamity, nor a headache, nor an illness except due to a sin; and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book:
And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.
He said: Then he said: And what Allah pardons is more than that for which He calls to account.

key_terms.عِرْقٍ: a vein; here, a bodily affliction or throbbing

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith teach that illnesses and hardships can be caused by sins?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that afflictions may occur as consequences of sins, and it supports this meaning by citing the Qur’anic verse that links calamities to what people have earned. At the same time, it emphasizes Allah’s mercy, stating that what Allah pardons is greater than what He holds people accountable for.
